Supply chain management covers the movement of products, information, and resources from suppliers to warehouses to customers. As data and operations grow, managing them efficiently becomes harder. This project applies appropriate data structures and a main algorithmic technique to improve supply chain management.

Manually managed systems struggle with data organization, inventory tracking, order processing, and delivery route selection. Searching and managing large volumes of suppliers, products, warehouses, and orders can become inefficient.

A structured system is needed to match each type of supply chain data with a suitable data structure. Linked Lists can manage dynamic supplier and product data, Queues can process orders in FIFO order, Binary Search Trees can organize inventory, and Graphs can represent warehouse and delivery connections. Binary Search supports efficient data retrieval.

The system manages and optimizes major supply chain activities — suppliers, products, inventory, warehouses, orders, and deliveries — using suitable data structures and algorithms.
A Linked List handles supplier and product records. A Queue processes orders (first-in, first-out).
A Binary Search Tree (BST) organizes inventory data. A Graph represents warehouses and delivery locations, with BFS exploring the network.
Binary Search locates products or suppliers quickly among sorted records.
Greedy selects efficient delivery options by choosing the nearest suitable warehouse at each step.
Supplier Management — Add, delete, update, and view supplier information.
Product and Inventory Management — Maintain product details and available stock.
Order Processing — Manage and process customer orders using a queue.
Warehouse Management — Organize inventory data using a binary search tree.
Delivery Network Management — Represent warehouses and delivery locations using graphs.
Route Exploration — Apply BFS to explore connections between locations.
Searching — Search for supplier, product, inventory, and order records efficiently.
Supply Chain Optimization — Apply the Greedy technique to solve warehouse-selection and delivery problems.
6. Data Structures and Algorithms to be Used
The system uses the following data structures and algorithms to manage suppliers, products, inventory, orders, warehouses, and delivery operations efficiently.
Manages dynamic data such as supplier details, product information, and inventory records, without needing a fixed size.
Insert: Add a new supplier, product, or inventory record.
Delete: Remove a record when no longer required.
Traverse: Display and access all records sequentially.
Handles customer order processing using the First-In, First-Out (FIFO) principle — the order placed first is processed first.
Organizes product or inventory records by a key such as Product ID — smaller values go to the left subtree, larger values to the right — enabling efficient search, insertion, and deletion.
Represents the delivery network: warehouses, suppliers, and delivery locations as vertices, and routes between them as edges. Implemented using an Adjacency List or Adjacency Matrix.
Explores the network level by level to identify connected locations and possible paths between warehouses and delivery points.
Searches sorted data efficiently by repeatedly dividing the search space in two — for example, finding a product by ID.
Selects the nearest available warehouse with sufficient stock to fulfil an order, making a locally optimal choice at each step to reduce delivery distance and cost.
